inputs.original_text: Phoenix leaders are calling the Wednesday-night vote “oversight,” but that sounds like cover for controlling both where federal immigration enforcement can operate and what the public is allowed to see. These restrictions don’t remove power; they put it in city officials’ hands, letting them decide the rules and manage the story. The accountability pitch is part of the maneuver, not a reason to take their explanation at face value.
inputs.modified_text: Phoenix leaders are dressing the Wednesday-night vote up as “oversight,” but the real move is to concentrate control: city officials get to shape where federal immigration enforcement can operate and what the public gets to see. The accountability language is there to make that power grab sound reasonable. When the people setting the limits also manage the story, their explanation deserves suspicion, not trust.
